sources.title: SFY 2026-2029 MORPC Transportation Improvement Program (full document)
sources.description: The full adopted TIP listing all federally funded transportation projects in the MORPC planning area for SFY 2026-2029, with funding sources per project.
sources.relevance: Master funding/prioritization document; the authoritative source for which projects are funded and how, covering all six pilot projects.
caveats: Some PDF pages contain little/no extractable text; see collection_status.json. Maps, figures, and table alignment require original-PDF review.

sources.title: Guide to the Transportation Improvement Program
sources.description: Plain-language explanation of how the TIP is developed, who is involved, and how projects are selected and prioritized.
sources.relevance: Explains the institutional decision process the platform needs to represent and explain to users.
caveats: Some PDF pages contain little/no extractable text; see collection_status.json. Maps, figures, and table alignment require original-PDF review.

sources.title: MORPC Transportation Improvement Program 2026-2029 Summary
sources.description: Plain-language summaries of all six pilot TIP projects in one place, written for public/community consumption, including the Renner Rd Park & Ride connection detail.
sources.relevance: Single-page cross-reference covering all six pilot projects; good candidate for an initial ingestion test.

sources.title: Roberts Rd at Frazell Rd and Spindler Rd Intersection Improvements - Fact Sheet
sources.description: Project scope: double compact urban roundabout construction, pedestrian/bicycle facilities, drainage, lighting.
sources.relevance: Primary project-specific source for Project #120250.

sources.title: Roberts Frazell Spindler Road Intersection - Crash History
sources.description: Crash statistics (17 crashes 2020-2022, 47% with injuries), 2013 study and 2020 feasibility study references, preferred alternative rationale.
sources.relevance: Direct evidence source for why this project was justified; good example of the evidence-tracing pattern the platform needs to support.

sources.title: Hilliard-Rome Road at Renner Road Intersection Improvements - Fact Sheet
sources.description: Project scope: intersection widening, lane reconfiguration, signal upgrades, adjacent intersection improvements.
sources.relevance: Primary project-specific source for Project #119852.

sources.title: Hilliard Rome Road at Renner Road - Intersection Safety Improvements
sources.description: Notes that this intersection is 'historically ranked high on MORPC's high crash list,' project rationale tied to nearby development.
sources.relevance: Evidence of MORPC's own prioritization language ('high crash list') applied to a specific project, useful precedent example.

sources.title: Alton & Darby Creek Road Closure - Roundabout Improvements
sources.description: June 2024 update about Cosgray/The Well area roundabouts; mismatched to original NP-37 tag.
sources.relevance: Excluded pending correct project source.
caveats: EXCLUDED: Article concerns Cosgray/The Well, Davis Road and Scioto Darby Road roundabouts; it does not establish the NP-37 Roberts Road project scope or status. Original association preserved only in original_inputs.

sources.title: Trabue Road Bridge Improvements Over IR-270 - Fact Sheet
sources.description: Bridge deck rehabilitation scope, ODOT-let project with City of Columbus funding contribution, shared-use path addition.
sources.relevance: Primary project-specific source for Project #120346.
caveats: Fact sheet identifies PID 105498. Crosswalk supported by full TIP PDF page 216: project 120346 states preliminary engineering is included with PID 105498. Preserve both identifiers; they are related, not interchangeable. Page 2 is a map with no extracted text.
Some PDF pages contain little/no extractable text; see collection_status.json. Maps, figures, and table alignment require original-PDF review.

sources.title: Trabue Road Bridge Improvements over IR-270
sources.description: Public-facing project description.
sources.relevance: Secondary confirmation source for Project #120346.

sources.title: Renner Road - Trabue Road - McKinley Avenue (RTMC) Mobility Study
sources.description: Corridor-level conceptual recommendations addressing mobility, economic vitality, health/safety, and employment access across the RTMC corridor. This is the underlying study behind both the Trabue Rd Shared Use Path (NP-125) and Renner Road path (NP-102) projects.
sources.relevance: The most important document for NP-125 and NP-102: no standalone fact sheet exists for these projects separate from this corridor study, so it is the primary evidence source for both.
caveats: Landing-page overview only. Full report and selected linked appendices are provided separately.

sources.title: RTMC Appendix K: Public Engagement
sources.description: Public comment summary; notes Trabue Road was the single most-commented-on location in the corridor (261 comments) regarding bike/ped facility requests.
sources.relevance: Direct evidence of community demand driving the Trabue Road SUP project; strong example for the evidence-tracing/stakeholder-input framework.
caveats: Some PDF pages contain little/no extractable text; see collection_status.json. Maps, figures, and table alignment require original-PDF review.

sources.title: Bike Plus 2025 Annual Report
sources.description: Status and mileage of current and upcoming bike/shared-use-path segments citywide, including specific Trabue Rd path segments.
sources.relevance: Cross-checks project status/mileage claims against the citywide active-transportation program.
caveats: Some PDF pages contain little/no extractable text; see collection_status.json. Maps, figures, and table alignment require original-PDF review.

sources.title: 2024-2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan (main page + chapters)
sources.description: 20-year regional transportation strategy; Chapter 7 (Project Evaluation & Fiscal Constraint) is directly relevant to prioritization logic; Appendices cover future land use, air quality, environmental justice, and environmental mitigation.
sources.relevance: The strategic backbone document; explains the criteria and goals against which individual TIP projects like the six pilots are justified.
caveats: Landing page, with nine linked chapters collected separately. Landing page calls linked PDFs adopted; filenames include Draft. Preserve this provenance rather than infer status from filenames.

sources.title: Vision Zero Columbus Action Plan 1.0 (ordinance + plan)
sources.description: Adopted city goal to eliminate fatal/serious-injury crashes by 2035; establishes Vision Zero as the primary safety framework.
sources.relevance: Core safety policy document; the goal against which all six pilot safety projects can be evaluated.
caveats: File is a Livingston Avenue grant appendix containing Vision Zero material and unrelated corridor material. Default chunks limited to the ordinance/action-plan portion.
Some PDF pages contain little/no extractable text; see collection_status.json. Maps, figures, and table alignment require original-PDF review.

sources.title: Vision Zero Columbus Action Plan 2023-2028
sources.description: Five-year implementation plan detailing strategies and actions under Vision Zero.
sources.relevance: Operational detail behind the Vision Zero policy goal.
caveats: Some PDF pages contain little/no extractable text; see collection_status.json. Maps, figures, and table alignment require original-PDF review.

sources.title: Vision Zero Columbus High Injury Network Map
sources.description: Interactive map of the High Injury Network (HIN), the roadway corridors with concentrated severe crashes.
sources.relevance: Directly joinable with the Columbus CoC Crash Data GIS layer (HIN, HIN_SEG_ID fields) in the companion GIS catalog; a strong candidate for combined text+spatial retrieval.
caveats: Interactive map: no useful static text. Use GIS catalog entry columbus_high_injury_network; relationship is thematic, underlying layer identity not revalidated.

sources.title: MTP 2024-2050 Appendix: Environmental Justice Technical Analysis
sources.description: MORPC's actual quantitative methodology for assessing whether transportation investments disproportionately affect or benefit low-income/minority populations, built on the travel demand forecasting model.
sources.relevance: This is the closest existing analog to the 'equity model' referenced in the original SOW; it documents MORPC's own assumptions and scoring approach, exactly the kind of institutional-memory content the platform needs to cite and explain.
caveats: PDF cover says DRAFT March 2024, Appendix D. MTP landing page lists this URL under Environmental Mitigation despite its Environmental Justice content. Version/appendix labeling is inconsistent; cite actual document title and qualify status.

sources.title: MORPC Environmental Justice Program Overview
sources.description: Overview of MORPC's three environmental justice principles and Title VI compliance approach.
sources.relevance: Policy-level framing for the more detailed EJ technical appendix.

sources.title: ODOT Traffic Engineering Manual, Section 800: Rail Grade Crossings
sources.description: Ohio's process for rail-highway crossing coordination: the ODOT/ORDC/PUCO/CSX/Norfolk Southern feasibility study committee, warning-time requirements, signal preemption rules.
sources.relevance: Explains the required coordination process for NP-125 (Trabue Road SUP, adjacent to Buckeye Yard/CSX-NS). Not region-specific, applies statewide, but directly governs this project's approval path.
caveats: Downloaded file contains Parts 8–15, not just rail crossings. Default chunks restricted to Part 8. Dated material: URL identifies a 2015 compilation; do not treat as verified current requirements. Project-specific applicability to NP-125 is unconfirmed.
Some PDF pages contain little/no extractable text; see collection_status.json. Maps, figures, and table alignment require original-PDF review.

sources.title: CSX Manual for Public Projects That May Involve the Railroad
sources.description: CSX's national process for coordinating with public agencies on projects near CSX property, including Quiet Zone procedures and required agreements.
sources.relevance: General national process document, not Columbus-specific, but directly applicable to NP-125 given Buckeye Yard is CSX/Norfolk Southern property.
caveats: Cover says last revised April 8, 2015. Historical reference, not verified current requirements. Project-specific applicability to NP-125 is unconfirmed.
Some PDF pages contain little/no extractable text; see collection_status.json. Maps, figures, and table alignment require original-PDF review.

sources.title: FHWA Railway-Highway Crossing Program Resources
sources.description: Federal guidance, noteworthy practices, and the Highway-Rail Crossing Handbook for grade-crossing safety planning.
sources.relevance: Background federal context for rail-crossing safety requirements; general, not Columbus-specific.
caveats: Direct download returned HTTP 403. Browser search could read the page, but it was not captured as a complete local original; excluded from local corpus.

sources.title: COTA Park & Ride Locations
sources.description: Confirms the Renner Rd Park & Ride location (5608 Renner Rd, Columbus), served by Lines 5 and 71.
sources.relevance: Direct confirmation source for the transit-access claim in Project NP-102.
caveats: Direct downloads timed out for both cota.com and www.cota.com. Browser search could read a cached PDF, but original bytes were not obtained; excluded from local corpus.
